chunks: And with this chain of narration from Ali ibn Harb [Al-Harith] from Al-Fadl ibn Yahya from his father from Abu 'Abdullah (AS), he said:

Visit Karbala and do not cut it off, for among the best offspring of the prophets, it has been included. Indeed, the angels visited Karbala a thousand years before my grandfather Husayn (AS) settled in it. And there is no night that place. And there is no night that passes except that Gabriel and Michael visit it. So strive, O Yahya, not to be deprived of that place.

key_terms.كَرْبَلَاءَ: Karbala, the city and shrine location of Imam Husayn (AS)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of visiting Karbala according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the cosmological significance of Karbala, portraying it not merely as a historical battlefield but as a sacred locus where the celestial realm intersects with the earthly. By highlighting the continuous visitation of Archangels Gabriel and Michael, the Imam establishes a precedent for the spiritual merit of Ziyarah, linking the physical act of pilgrimage to the eternal worship of the angels. This narrative reinforces the Shia belief in the sanctity of the Imams' resting places as focal points of divine presence and intercession.
